summary: The tape was loud at index level and quiet for the held single names. Alphabet fell about 12% on AI-capex fears, Amazon and Intel slid after earnings, and the Fed held with hawkish talk; VOO and VTI lost about 1.6% and the account gave back $2.18 (-0.4%), well ahead of SPY on the day. No headline, 8-K 4.01/4.02/5.02 or 1.01/2.01 hit any held single stock today. IDXX fell 4.3% with no IDXX headline or filing in the input, so the cause is unexplained by the news and may be the Intel/Dell tech-hardware selloff or sector rotation; it is unverified. The one real news event for a holding is the record Binance hack (about $6.3B, plus a Trezor hardware-tampering alert): BTC fell about 3% to $77k but was +0.27% on the day at the close, so the exchange-failure risk was absorbed. Lesson L2 held up: every held name's earnings date was checked against filings (INCY, HWM, LNG, BDC, EXEL, GRMN, LOGI, EXLS, RRC all show 8-K 2.02 or 10-Q, so their stale estimates are resolved). Still open: the WMT 8-K 8.01 from 10-23 is unread (the input shows only item numbers) and ages out of the 7-day window today or tomorrow. Today's WMT headline, a roughly $6B Symbotic automation deal across 25 distribution centers, is supportive, and WMT was +1.9%.

broken_theses.why: The 10-21 invalidation reads 'an exchange failure or adverse regulatory action appears in the news'. The record Binance hack (10-29, about $6.3B, called the largest crypto heist) is an exchange security failure and arguably meets that wording literally. It did not break the price: BTC is about -3% on the hack, still -8.2% on cost (inside the 10% stop) and +0.27% on the day, and Binance has not failed as a venue. This is a judgment call rather than a clear break; the PM should either say explicitly that a hack that the venue survives does not trip the clause or treat it as tripped. Related negatives that are opinion, not events: Strategy paused BTC buying, analysts warn of a $73k-$76k test, and Kevin O'Leary says the CLARITY Act may not lift BTC and may stall after the midterms.

Not broken, but a premise has lapsed. The 10-22 thesis rested on earnings 11-05 being outside the 5-day window. The company confirmed 11-05 after the close (headline 10-29), which is now 4 trading days out, and the first reaction day (11-06) is the fifth. The thesis's own invalidation (a negative earnings surprise inside the next five trading days) is now live on a 5.1% position that fell 1.0% today with no CARG-specific news.

upcoming: Mon 11-02 is the key date. It has had two sell-side PT cuts (Jefferies, UBS) and a 4.3% drop today with no news, and the PM earlier judged the stress loss tolerable. CLX (not held) is also estimated 11-02 and filed an 8-K 5.02 (officer change, unread) on 10-29, with negative preview drift. CARG reports 11-05 after the close (confirmed by the company); the date is 4 trading days out. Other nearby prints are not held: EXEL 11-03 (the 10-29 8-K 2.02 and results show it already reported, so the estimate is stale), MTCH, ULS and GPOR around 11-03 (ULS and GPOR own dates unverified), SMG company-confirmed 11-04, and DBX, TPR, RL and ONC 11-05. Macro and crypto: Friday's Alphabet, Amazon and Intel selloff and the Dell/HP warning on PC demand and memory shortages (Apple-tagged, no AAPL filing) keep the AI-capex thread alive for QQQ-linked holdings; the Fed holds at 3.75-4.00% with a December hike priced (IEF/BND risk is two-sided on the duration side); BTC support levels cited are $76.3k and $73k, and midterm headlines are an overhang. CART (not held) was hit by five downgrades after the DoorDash $17B deal 8-K 1.01, a deal-gap signal only. DPZ: Johnson Fistel announced a derivative-claims investigation (10-28); law-firm notices have not led to filings so far, so it is noise until an 8-K or complaint appears, as with the earlier MLI notice. WMT's 8-K 8.01 from 10-23 will likely age out of the window unread; no further action is possible from this input.
